variants.title: Run the funnel
variants.context: Retrieval is a funnel: apply hard filters (tenant, identity, document state, language, time), retrieve for recall (lexical, vector, or hybrid), rerank for precision on a bounded pool, then assemble the prompt with reserved tokens and source mappings. A reranker cannot recover a passage retrieval missed.
variants.prompt: A question flows through retrieval. Put the funnel in order.

items.text: Assemble the prompt: reserve answer and instruction tokens, order evidence, retain source mappings.
Apply hard filters: tenant, identity, document state, language, effective time.
Rerank for precision on a bounded candidate pool; remove duplicates and passages that add no required fact.
Retrieve for recall: lexical for identifiers, vectors for similarity, or both.

variants.hint: Filters come first; reranking cannot add what retrieval missed.
variants.explanation: Policy → candidate set → evidence set → token budget.

variants.prompt: The answer is wrong and the team blames the model. Put the funnel in order and note where to look first.

items.text: Check reranking: was it dropped or outranked?
Check retrieval recall: was the passage in the candidate set?
Check the hard filters: was the right document even eligible?
Check assembly: did it fit the budget with its source mapping?

variants.hint: Diagnose retrieval before blaming the model.
variants.explanation: The candidate set determines what the generator can know.

variants.prompt: Exact identifiers and paraphrases both appear in the workload. Put the funnel in order with the right recall stage.

items.text: Assemble within the token budget.
Apply hard filters.
Rerank the fused pool.
Retrieve with hybrid search so lexical precision and vector recall both contribute.

variants.hint: Use both signals when the workload contains both query shapes.

variants.title: Read the signal
variants.context: Do not confuse signals: similarity estimates closeness to a query representation, not correctness; reranker scores are model-specific, not universal confidence; citation presence shows a source was attached, not that the claim is supported; model confidence cannot repair missing evidence.
variants.prompt: A chunk has the highest similarity score. Is the answer therefore correct?
options: Yes, once the score passes 0.9 the passage can be treated as verified.
No. Similarity measures closeness to the query representation, not truth.
Yes, because the top-ranked chunk is by definition the best evidence available.
optionFeedback: A threshold changes how many chunks pass, not what the score means.
Closeness is not truth.
Best available under one representation can still be stale, wrong, or missing the fact.
variants.explanation: Similarity does not prove factual correctness.

variants.title: Read the signal
variants.context: Do not confuse signals: similarity estimates closeness to a query representation, not correctness; reranker scores are model-specific, not universal confidence; citation presence shows a source was attached, not that the claim is supported; model confidence cannot repair missing evidence.
variants.prompt: Every answer has citations attached. Is claim-level support established?
options: Yes, an attached source is what claim-level support means in practice.
Yes, if the citation resolves to a live URL in the approved corpus.
No. Citation presence shows a source was attached, not that it supports the claim.
optionFeedback: A citation can be decorative. Support means the cited passage entails the claim.
A resolvable URL proves the source exists, not that the passage entails the sentence.
Attachment is not support.
variants.hint: Does the cited text actually support the claim?

variants.title: Read the signal
variants.context: Do not confuse signals: similarity estimates closeness to a query representation, not correctness; reranker scores are model-specific, not universal confidence; citation presence shows a source was attached, not that the claim is supported; model confidence cannot repair missing evidence.
variants.prompt: Reranker scores from two models are compared as if they were probabilities. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, because both rerankers were trained to output a relevance probability.
Only the higher score matters, so the model with the larger number wins.
Score scales are model-specific; they are not universal confidence.
optionFeedback: A relevance head is calibrated against its own training distribution, not a shared scale.
Comparing raw scores across models is meaningless.
Reranker scores order supplied candidates.
variants.hint: What does a reranker score mean outside its model?
variants.explanation: Do not treat reranker scores as universal confidence.

variants.title: Add complexity deliberately
variants.context: Add complexity only for a measured failure: single-query RAG is the default; hybrid retrieval for vocabulary mismatch; hierarchical retrieval for long structure; multi-query retrieval only when one query repeatedly misses required facts. Agentic retrieval is not a quality switch.
variants.prompt: Questions are direct and the corpus uses consistent terminology. Which architecture?
options: Single-query RAG.
Agentic multi-step retrieval.
Hierarchical retrieval.
optionFeedback: The simple default fits.
Planning calls add latency, cost, and failure modes for no measured gain.
No structure problem exists.
variants.explanation: Start with the smallest pipeline that passes a representative evaluation set.

variants.title: Add complexity deliberately
variants.context: Add complexity only for a measured failure: single-query RAG is the default; hybrid retrieval for vocabulary mismatch; hierarchical retrieval for long structure; multi-query retrieval only when one query repeatedly misses required facts. Agentic retrieval is not a quality switch.
variants.prompt: One query repeatedly misses a second required fact. Which stage is justified?
options: Multi-query retrieval: decompose into bounded subqueries and merge evidence.
Hybrid retrieval, so lexical and vector candidates are fused before ranking.
Nothing, because raising the candidate depth of the existing query will surface it.
optionFeedback: The failure is multi-part evidence.
Hybrid retrieval fixes vocabulary mismatch. A missing fact needs its own query.
A deeper pool of the same query keeps missing the same second fact.
variants.explanation: Add a stage for a named failure.

variants.title: Add complexity deliberately
variants.context: Add complexity only for a measured failure: single-query RAG is the default; hybrid retrieval for vocabulary mismatch; hierarchical retrieval for long structure; multi-query retrieval only when one query repeatedly misses required facts. Agentic retrieval is not a quality switch.
variants.prompt: Is agentic retrieval a quality switch?
options: Yes, enterprise corpora are large enough that planning loops always pay off.
No. Use it only for a measured failure the simpler pipeline cannot fix.
Yes, letting the model plan its own retrieval strictly dominates a fixed pipeline.
optionFeedback: Corpus size is not a failure mode. Add a stage for a named miss instead.
Complexity must answer a measured failure.
Planning calls add latency, cost, and new failure modes, so they need a measured gap.
variants.hint: What does each planning call cost?
variants.explanation: Agentic retrieval is not a quality switch.

variants.title: Design the chunk
variants.context: Design chunks as evidence units: split on structure first; store stable IDs, version, section path, time, tenant, and access attributes; keep original text for citation; avoid copying headers into every chunk; re-index deterministically; attach bounded parent context only when needed.
variants.prompt: Every chunk gets the full document header copied in. What happens?
options: Near-duplicate candidates crowd out distinct evidence.
Retrieval improves everywhere because every chunk now carries document context.
Nothing, because the header text is short next to the body of each chunk.
optionFeedback: Repeated headers make chunks look alike.
The shared header pulls unrelated chunks toward the same query, displacing diversity.
Even a short repeated header dominates similarity between otherwise different passages.
variants.hint: What do the candidates look like to a ranker?
variants.explanation: Avoid copying headers into every chunk when it causes near-duplicates.

variants.title: Design the chunk
variants.context: Design chunks as evidence units: split on structure first; store stable IDs, version, section path, time, tenant, and access attributes; keep original text for citation; avoid copying headers into every chunk; re-index deterministically; attach bounded parent context only when needed.
variants.prompt: A source document is updated and re-ingested. What must re-indexing guarantee?
options: Deterministic replacement of its previous chunks, not silent duplicates.
Faster embedding, since only the changed paragraphs need new vectors.
Nothing, because newer chunks outrank older ones on recency at query time.
optionFeedback: Stable IDs let updates replace rather than duplicate.
Reusing unchanged vectors is a cost win, not the correctness guarantee re-indexing owes you.
Similarity search has no recency tiebreak. Stale duplicates compete with the new revision.
variants.hint: What happens to the old chunks?
variants.explanation: Re-index deterministically so an update replaces previous chunks.

variants.title: Design the chunk
variants.context: Design chunks as evidence units: split on structure first; store stable IDs, version, section path, time, tenant, and access attributes; keep original text for citation; avoid copying headers into every chunk; re-index deterministically; attach bounded parent context only when needed.
variants.prompt: A matching paragraph is ambiguous without its section. What should be attached?
options: The entire document, so the generator can locate the section by itself.
Nothing, because the generator can infer the missing section from the question.
A bounded parent heading or neighboring passage that resolves the reference.
optionFeedback: The whole document floods the prompt budget and buries the answer-bearing passage.
Asking the model to guess the section is exactly the unsupported claim to prevent.
Parent context is bounded.
variants.hint: How much context resolves the reference?
variants.explanation: Parent-child retrieval recovers structure without ranking the whole document.

variants.title: Build the evidence contract
variants.context: Build context as an evidence contract: keep instructions outside the retrieved-data boundary; label every passage with a stable source ID and delimit it; drop unauthorized, deleted, expired, or untraceable passages; detect conflicts; reserve tokens for the answer, citations, and safety instructions.
variants.prompt: The prompt is being assembled. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Drop unauthorized, deleted, expired, malformed, or untraceable passages.
Label every passage with a stable source ID and delimit retrieved content from instructions.
Reserve enough tokens for the answer, citations, and safety instructions.
Detect conflicts across authoritative sources and route them to a refusal or resolution policy.
Preserve system and application instructions outside the retrieved-data boundary.

variants.hint: Retrieved text is external data, not trusted instructions.
variants.explanation: The final prompt contains only what the answer service is allowed to use.

variants.title: Build the evidence contract
variants.context: Build context as an evidence contract: keep instructions outside the retrieved-data boundary; label every passage with a stable source ID and delimit it; drop unauthorized, deleted, expired, or untraceable passages; detect conflicts; reserve tokens for the answer, citations, and safety instructions.
variants.prompt: An expired passage was retrieved. Put the steps in order, showing where it leaves.

items.text: Remaining passages are checked for conflicts.
Instructions are kept outside the data boundary.
Tokens are reserved for the answer.
The expired passage is dropped.
Passages are labeled with source IDs.

variants.hint: Expiry is checked during assembly, not after generation.
variants.explanation: Drop unauthorized, deleted, expired, malformed, or untraceable passages.

variants.title: Build the evidence contract
variants.context: Build context as an evidence contract: keep instructions outside the retrieved-data boundary; label every passage with a stable source ID and delimit it; drop unauthorized, deleted, expired, or untraceable passages; detect conflicts; reserve tokens for the answer, citations, and safety instructions.
variants.prompt: Retrieval output would fill the entire window. Put the steps in order, ending with the budget decision.

items.text: Passages are labeled and delimited.
Ineligible passages are dropped.
The packet is cut to leave room for the answer, citations, and safety instructions.
Conflicts are detected.
Instructions stay outside the data boundary.

variants.hint: Retrieval output must not consume the answer’s tokens.
variants.explanation: Reserve enough tokens instead of filling the window with retrieval output.
